cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Could You Just…
cards.instruction: Turn a difficult task into tiny favors until the help quietly becomes most of the task.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Could you pinch these bouquet stems together? My wedding ribbon keeps sliding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've got them. You need wire underneath.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Could you twist this bit round, just where your fingers are?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There. That sharp end will snag the dress.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tuck it in and wind the ribbon over it? One little bow would hide everything. I'll hold the scissors.

mechanism: A claims bouquet-making expertise while asking for one small correction after another until B does the binding and final presentation.
confusable: Generic bossiness demands the whole task openly; D25 needs the expanding labour to be framed as tiny favors.
comparison: Shelf alternative exploits time-saving fastening; bouquet alternative uses safety and finish flaws B notices.
seedUse: Stems, wire snag and ribbon derive from D25-b; S03 adds alignment, binding and finished-bow corrections to the quiet transfer of labour.
